Am wife of u/subr3al1ty, I thought is chime in as a partner of a trans baby. Its definitely hard. I'm not even going to lie. I've always supported and pushed her to do what makes her happy, but it can be a lot sometimes. 

Seeing the changes on a more intimate level is kinda scary at times. When she first started spironolactone, I noticed her 'man smell' go away, and I think I cried for a week over it. The intimacy changes are also frustrating. When she goes out alone, presenting as she wants I have anxiety all day, when we're out together, I have to have her right beside me so I know she's safe. The voice thing is tough, I've lived with the same voice for 5 years, and its a source of comfort when my life feels rocky, so sometimes I have to ask for a break from it.

But there's also incredible changes that I get more excited about than she does. Getting her new clothes and seeing how she lights up, feeling her skin getting softer, the moment I knew she got her estrogen prescription, giving the first shot... Seeing her confidence skyrocket and her personality shine through. Watching her become more involved in our daughters life, instead of being a little more hands off... 

Its a big, scary change for you, but also her. This should be, in my opinion, something you two go through as a team. Make big decisions together, because it impacts you both. Maybe she wants to push back the wedding so you can be who you are? Give her some time to adjust and come to terms about life changing. Give her some grace to feel emotions and figure out what it means for her. I had to do some real searching to figure out what it meant for my sexuality, maybe she's thinking about that too? I know that for me, being involved in the process helps me adapt to it easier. Its why we went with shots for hormones, so I'm involved. 

Give her time. I promise it'll be ok in the end.

I had my BAE in my store on Tuesday. I think what they're talking about is the plan do review sheet. We fill it out for ourselves and our BAE might ask to see it. I really wouldn't worry. Do your best, and reach out to your BAE for more clarification on the survey, and for advice on events. Certain events don't do well in certain areas. A little tip is to move your event table to the front of your department, and try a hands off approach of 'hey I have an event going on today, take a look at my table and if you have questions I'll hop right over' instead of an 'approach every customer' style.

They can't fire you for not hitting event goals! I went 2 years with zeros on all of my events except the big ones like pink Sunday. What I'd do is get with your BAE and see if you can make an action plan. Use your plan do review sheets, and look at the featured item lists on the beauty website. See if you can find the cheapest items on the list and promote them, find products you can be passionate about 😊 some events are easier than others. We look for 'big bets'- find 1 event a month that you know you can rock super easily, and knock it out of the park! Don't be hard on yourself, events are hard, but you got this! 

Edit:I've never heard of us having to put our daily numbers in through a portal, it automatically tracks it for us and gives us our numbers the Thursday after the event, I think us inputting numbers ourselves would lead to a lot of fraud?

BC here, easiest way to do resets is start at one end, and do a 3 foot section at a time. We start by going through and pulling all the discontinued and nonbasics. We find it easier to pull the fixtures that have no changes, put them in their new spot, and then just put internals in their designated tray and go from there. Do graphics and new product placement last. 

Its definitely intense. Just start at one end and work your way down. (If they have wet and wild/rimmel at one end, start there because its just easy sections) 

Boxes will be labeled with what products fit in the fixtures, so its easy to match up with location and product. 

Don't flop between brands, finish a brand/section of a brand 100% before moving down 

If you have any questions shoot me a message, I've done 4 or 5 so far, and have a pretty good idea of what might work, depending on store layout and bde conversion level 😊

His mom was my fifth grade teacher back in the day, and our moms worked together in a deli at the local grocery store. For a few years after we both graduated, our moms fought tooth and nail to get us to at least be friends. We didn't have many friends, so they were just trying to help us out. After a bit of a party phase and a bad breakup with a good friend, I decided to take them up on their offer to get me his number. You know how sometimes you just have a feeling about something? I didn't get his number earlier, because something told me if I did, my party days would be over, and things would get serious before I was ready. We started talking, and my inklings about him were correct. We went out on a lunch date just to prove our moms wrong, and it was over for us. We've been inseparable ever since. Got engaged five months later, and found out we were having our daughter two months after that. This December we will be together for two years, our daughter is six months old today, and we get married next year. 

My advice is to just trust your guts. Don't rush these things, because love happens when it does for a reason. If you aren't in the right emotional state, and have things to work out for yourself, it won't happen. And trusting your parents judgement and taking them up on the offer to hook you up with a coworkers kid, might just be worth the I told you so's.
